concept: Same visual language as the approved File Harbor dashboard. Cover the rest of the product. No illustration, avatars, storage totals, or fake analytics. Operator name is a text string. Theme control is system/light/dark. Admin shell stays: wordmark, operator identity, theme, sign out; left rail with inventory, status filters, create actions. Sibling screens: - Login: username and password, short aside on what File Harbor is (self-hosted, links not accounts, files go to your storage). - New receive link: label, optional password, max uploads, expiry. - New send link: label, optional password, max downloads, expiry, file picker/drop. - Receive link detail: share URL, status, policy, file list, disable, delete. - Send link detail: share URL, status, policy, files with download counts, disable, delete. - Notifications: list of upload/download events, mark read. - Public receive /r/7K2M: visitor uploads a file; password if required; progress; no admin chrome. - Public send /s/9QWX: visitor downloads files; password if required; remaining downloads; no admin chrome. Public pages drop the rail and counts. Keep proportional type, sentence-case, green accent, light-first.
sitePurpose: Create self-hosted links for collecting and delivering files through your own storage.
statusUpdate: I’ll extend the dashboard into the essential link-creation, management, notification, sign-in, and visitor transfer routes. Together, these routes let operators configure file exchanges and let recipients upload or download without needing an account.
approvedScreenSummary: The approved source shows the signed-in All links inventory, with link type, labels, codes, status, expiry, usage, and creation dates; filtering, search, bulk actions, status counts, and actions to create receive or send links are already present.

pages.title: All links
pages.purpose: Give an operator a searchable, filterable inventory of existing receive and send links and entry points to create more.

pages.title: Sign in
pages.purpose: Authenticate an operator and briefly explain the product’s self-hosted, link-based file exchange model.

pages.title: New receive link
pages.purpose: Configure a link that permits visitors to upload files into the operator’s storage.

pages.title: Receive link: Press kit
pages.purpose: Manage the active Press kit receive link and review the files submitted through it.

pages.title: New send link
pages.purpose: Prepare a controlled download link by selecting files and defining its access policy.

screens.content: Provide username and password fields, sign-in feedback, and a concise explanation that File Harbor creates links rather than user accounts and sends received files directly to the operator’s storage.
Collect a recognizable label, optional password, maximum upload count, and expiry choice. Confirm the intended receive policy before the operator creates the link.

Show the share URL for code 7K2M, active status, expiry, password and upload-limit policy, and a file list with submitted press materials. Offer controls to copy the link, disable it, or permanently delete it.
Collect a label, optional password, maximum download count, and expiry choice, then let the operator add files through a picker or drop area before creating the send link.
